issues.legal_issue: A descendant of a grantee of territory acquired by conquest does not inherit the former sovereign’s rights merely by descent from that grantee.
material_facts: The territory had belonged to an independent ruler whose sovereign rights included rights in royal trees.
After conquest, the territory passed to the conquering rulers, and a jagir within it was granted to the claimant’s ancestor.
The claimant was a descendant of the jagirdar, not a successor to the independent sovereign.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not establish ownership of the trees by relying on the sovereign rights of the former independent rulers.
issues.legal_principle: On acquisition of territory by a sovereign state, inhabitants may assert in municipal courts only rights recognized by the new sovereign; rights held under the former rulers do not by themselves survive. The Court applied Vajesingji Joravarsingji v. Secretary of State for India ([1924] L.R. 51 I.A. 357).

predicates.civil_title_claim: A claimant brings a civil proceeding to establish ownership of property.
predicates.territory_acquired_by_conquest: The territory containing the property passed to a new sovereign through conquest.
predicates.claimant_derives_from_grantee_not_former: The claimant derives title from a grantee under the new sovereign rather than as a successor to the former sovereign.

issues.definition: When a civil title claim concerns territory acquired by conquest and the claimant derives title from a grantee rather than the former sovereign, the claimant cannot claim the former sovereign’s rights on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: A grant primarily assigning land revenue does not transfer unmentioned sovereign rights in trees on the cultivated and proprietary lands of subjects.
material_facts: The grant described villages and their revenue and provided that the grantee could receive revenue from the subjects according to the governing rules.
The grant restricted the grantee from collecting other specified dues and did not expressly grant rights to trees on the subjects’ cultivated and proprietary lands.
The claimant relied on the grant to assert ownership of pine trees on those lands.
issues.conclusion: The grant did not give the claimant or his predecessor the right to the pine trees on the respondents’ cultivated and proprietary lands.
issues.legal_principle: Grants made by a sovereign are generally construed most favourably to the sovereign. Where the intention is clear, the grant receives a fair and liberal interpretation; a plainly expressed operative term may prevail over qualifications in recitals. A grant for valuable consideration, and one capable of a valid or void construction, may be construed in favour of the grantee and in a manner that preserves its validity. Applying these principles, the Court construed the grant as primarily an assignment of land revenue and found no transfer of the claimed tree rights.

predicates.grant_scope_dispute: A claimant relies on a sovereign grant to establish ownership of property.
predicates.grant_assigns_revenue_from_subjects: The grant assigns revenue from subjects or villages to the grantee.
predicates.grant_does_not_expressly_transfer_tree_r: The grant does not expressly transfer rights in trees on the subjects’ cultivated and proprietary lands.

issues.definition: Where a grant-scope dispute concerns a grant assigning revenue from subjects without expressly transferring tree rights on their cultivated and proprietary lands, the grant does not transfer those claimed tree rights.

issues.legal_issue: Entries in a village administration record cannot create title to a sovereign right or establish its surrender when they do not record an existing custom and do not unambiguously show surrender.
material_facts: The claimant relied on entries in village administration records stating that pine trees in the holdings of inferior proprietors belonged to the superior landlord.
The records did not identify an existing village custom supporting that right, and the asserted right had been a sovereign right.
The entries did not unambiguously show that the sovereign had surrendered or relinquished the right; other land records did not record the claimed restriction on the proprietors’ rights.
The claimant’s case did not establish the asserted tree ownership independently of those entries.
issues.conclusion: The entries did not establish an existing custom, a grant or surrender of the sovereign right, or title to the trees in the claimant.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 31 and 44 of the Punjab Land-Revenue Act, 1887, the village administration paper forms part of the record of rights and its entries are presumed true. Such a record records existing rights and customs; it cannot create new rights or liabilities. The presumption may be displaced according to the facts of the case. The Court relied on Dakas Khan v. Ghulam Kasim Khan (A.I.R. 1918 P.C. 4), which states that an entry does not create title but gives rise to a rebuttable presumption, and Gurbakhsh Singh v. Mst. Partapo ([1921] I.L.R. 2 Lah. 346), concerning the authority of village-specific revenue records. It also relied on Rajah Venkata Narasimha Appa Row Bahadur v. Rajah Narayya Appa Row Bahadur ([1879] L.R. 7 I.A. 38) for the proposition that revenue officials’ views on the construction or effect of a grant do not bind civil courts.

predicates.property_title_claim_based_on_village_re: A claimant seeks to establish property ownership on the basis of an entry in a village administration record.
predicates.record_entry_asserts_sovereign_right_in_: The entry attributes to the claimant a right that was formerly held as a sovereign right.
predicates.no_evidenced_existing_custom: The evidence does not show that the entry records an existing custom of the village.
predicates.no_unambiguous_surrender: The entry does not clearly show that the sovereign surrendered or relinquished the right to the claimant or the claimant’s predecessor.

issues.definition: If a property title claim based on a village record relies on an entry asserting a sovereign right, but no existing custom or unambiguous surrender is shown, the entry does not establish title to that right.
